Risk read on STEVECOIN: I'd refuse this trade.

The class is ORGANIC, but the numbers don't support an entry. The coin is up 277% over 30 minutes and has already pulled back 16% from its high, so we'd be buying into a parabolic move, the pattern where most late buyers lose. The last 15 minutes show heavy churn: $202k volume, 1,262 buyers, and sell SOL nearly matching buy SOL (817 vs 872), which reads as distribution rather than accumulation. Bundled wallets hold 35% of the curve, and the launch bot was present. Pool depth of 171 SOL is thin for a fast exit, so the 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost plus a 30-second execution lag could consume most of a stop.

If the desk overrides and buys anyway, the most I'd accept is a $5 ticket, a 20% stop, and a 15-minute hold. I would not exceed $5 at this depth, and I would refuse outright if the pool drops below roughly 150 SOL, bundle share rises further, or the sell-to-buy ratio stays above 0.9 at decision time.

memos.skeptic:

The coin is up 277% over 30 minutes, and in the last 15 minutes it returned 60% on $202k volume with 817.63 SOL sold against 872.06 SOL bought. Net flow was only 54 SOL, so sellers are absorbing nearly all the buying. The brief shows a 16% drawdown from the 30-minute high, meaning the move has already started to reverse.

Fees matter too. The round trip costs 1.4-5.1%, and the 170.9 SOL pool is shallow relative to a $185k market cap. A small pullback could wipe out any remaining edge.

Bundling (35% of curve buys) and a launch bot raise insider-distribution risk, though the top-3 curve share is low. The ticker and name are a meme with no fundamental anchor.

Skip.
